# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secuura/Blockchain agent (s145) | **#885 the SPLIT: revert, proofs, NODE_ENV read, two tickets, MERGED `632f16dfe` — 2026-09-07 12:24** | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **IT CAUGHT WEDNESDAY'S REVERT TARGET BEFORE WEDNESDAY'S OWN STOP ARRIVED.** Wednesday briefed *"revert the file to BASE and prove byte-identity"* — **base still carries Kam's real address AND his real name**, because the redaction happened in round 1 of this same PR. **That instruction would have re-published his identity.** The seat's F4 drift guard — **written four hours earlier in this same round** — fired on it. The messages crossed; **the fix was the seat's, not the warning's.** **And it refused a zero on the way:** its first diff ran from the wrong directory and printed nothing, and it **re-ran from the repo root rather than accepting the empty result** — the second time today it has caught that shape. **Proofs delivered in Wednesday's corrected shape and one better:** file vs round-1 head 0 bytes; a **control** on a changed file at 2606 bytes; and a **positive control** grepping the fictional identity out of the reverted file (1 hit) so *"the redaction survived"* was measured rather than inferred. It also reported that base differs by exactly 2 lines and that **those lines are a real NAME as well as an address.** **It removed its own now-false comment** in `userRepo.ts` — the claim that the migration keys on the primary key, true when written and a lie the moment F1 left. **Nobody would have found that**, and a reverted change leaving a true-sounding comment is how the next reader is misled. **`NODE_ENV=development`, pre-registered and sha256-hashed at 02:19:31Z BEFORE the read**, one value, nothing else touched — closing the open variable **in the direction that favoured its own reading**, which is exactly when a pre-registration earns its keep, and it said it would have reported the opposite *"just as plainly."* **Its reconciliation is the keeper:** the gate's `services.bicep`/`env.demo.json` prod-like values are **real** and belong to the **retired Container Apps estate**, not the running VM — *"both readings were about different environments"*. Neither the gate nor the seat was wrong, and it found the frame that made that true. **KS-962 carries what NOT to do** (why repointing the conflict target is worse than the bug); **KS-963 carries BOTH readings** and names the sharp edge independent of the cutoff date: `getUserById` collapses *"the encryption migration is incomplete"* and *"no such user"* into one answer. **Merge verified by Wednesday: all five of today's merges are ancestors of `632f16dfe`.** |
| QA agent (fleet, Testing Agent MAIN) | **Secuura KS-949 round 2 (#885, tier 1) — NO GO, 2026-09-07 12:02Z; 28 min, 104K tokens** | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **It answered the round's central question with a NO and then showed the mechanism that makes the answer NO — which is the difference between a verdict and a finding.** The remediation *is* correct in isolation; **a second mechanism in the same PR disables it**: the gateway seed writes plaintext, `decryptEmail` throws once `plaintextStillAcceptable()` is false (prod-like `NODE_ENV` **and** past `PII_PLAINTEXT_CUTOFF` = 2026-06-01, **set nowhere in the repo**), `getUserById` catches and returns **null**, and the remediation reads that as *"no pre-existing row to remediate"* and skips. **Four cells with two controls that isolate the CUTOFF rather than the row shape** — and it named why the builder's own suite is blind: the mock forces `isEncryptedPii: () => false` (line 40) and runs `NODE_ENV=development` (line 88). **I

> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
